Present Monitoring in the Project Area - In addition to the ground-water monitoring network established in Tract III by Montana Bureau of Mines and Geology (Van Voast and Hedges, 1974), Westmoreland Resources has initiated a ground-water monitoring program in Tracts II and III. The program is designed to obtain baseline chemical and physical characteristics of the ground water in the project area (Westmoreland Resources, 1975 1). This network includes a selected number of the 43 observation wells within and around the project area. Ground-water quality data are given in Tables 11 and 12.
Observation wells in the Rosebud-McKay overburden and coal, Robinson coal, and the upper Sub-Robinson unit were sampled during the summer and fall of 1974 and 1975. Wells in valley alluvium were sampled in the summer and fall of 1975. Westmoreland Resources (1975 1) provides the following description of the ground water of the mining area during July and October 1974 and August 1975:
Dissolved solids and evaporated solids concentrations range from 75 mg/l in the Rosebud-McKay overburden to 2,700 mg/l in the Robinson coal, indicating increasing concentrations with depth. Likewise, in general, the lowest concentrations of sulfate (about 130 mg/l to 500 mg/l) occur in the stratigraphically high zones on Tract III, the Rosebud-McKay Coal and overburden, and the Robinson Coal on Tract II.
